title: Holomorphic structures in the low-discriminant non-algebraic case
statement_utf8:
Let $X$ be a non-algebraic complex surface and let $E$ be a differentiable rank-$r$ complex vector bundle on $X$ with $c_1(E)\in NS(X)$. Writing
\[
\Delta(E)=2r c_2(E)-(r-1)c_1(E)^2
\]
and
\[
m(r,c)=r\inf\left\{-\sum_{i=1}^r\left(\frac{c}{r}-\mu_i\right)^2\;\middle|\;\mu_i\in NS(X),\ \sum_{i=1}^r\mu_i=c\right\},
\]
determine whether bundles satisfying
\[
0\leq \Delta(E)<m(r,c_1(E))
\]
admit holomorphic structures. Any such holomorphic structure, if it exists, is necessarily non-filtrable.
technical_disposition: All non-algebraic surfaces and ranks are quantified. The discriminant interval alone gives no elementary existence construction; non-filtrability is only a necessary conclusion. PARK geometric existence, not a finite certificate.

title: Natural direct-limit C*-algebra for a general curved Hilbert manifold
statement_utf8:
For a general curved Hilbert manifold $M$ with Riemannian metric $g$, construct a natural direct-limit $C^*$-algebra
$$
\mathcal A(M)=\varinjlim_{M_a\subset M}\mathcal A(M_a),
\qquad
\mathcal A(M_a)=C_0(\mathbb R)\widehat\otimes\mathcal C(M_a)
\cong C_0(\mathbb R)\widehat\otimes C_0\!\left(M_a,\operatorname{Cliff}(TM_a)\right),
$$
where the direct limit is taken over finite-dimensional submanifolds $M_a\subset M$, by defining compatible connecting maps for smooth (isometric) inclusions $M_a\subset M_b\subset M$ so that the required diagrams commute.

title: The lattice covering problem in every dimension
statement_utf8:
For each integer $d\ge 1$, let $B_d$ be the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For a full-rank discrete subgroup (lattice) $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, define

\]
and determine all lattices $L$ attaining this minimum.

title: $L^1$-optimal Dirichlet boundary control of a string to rest in finite time
statement_utf8:
Given $T>0$, $L>0$, $c>0$, and initial data $y_0,y_1$, consider

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{u_1,u_2\in L^1(0,T)}\quad &\int_0^T \bigl(|u_1(t)|+|u_2(t)|\bigr)\,dt\\
\text{subject to}\quad &y_{tt}(x,t)=c^2y_{xx}(x,t), &&(x,t)\in(0,L)\times(0,T),\\
&y(0,t)=u_1(t),\quad y(L,t)=u_2(t), &&t\in(0,T),\\
&y(x,0)=y_0(x),\quad y_t(x,0)=y_1(x), &&x\in(0,L),\\
&y(x,T)=0,\quad y_t(x,T)=0, &&x\in(0,L).
\end{aligned}
$$

The report states that, under $T\ge t_0=L/c$, $y_0\in L^1(0,L)$, and $Y_1(x)=\int_0^x y_1(s)\,ds\in L^1(0,L)$, Theorem 1 explicitly describes all optimal controls, gives the minimum as $I(r)$ for a minimizing real number $r$, and states that the solution is unique if and only if this minimum is zero.

title: The Big Z: optimal deterministic programming of POVMs
statement_utf8:
For a system of dimension $d$, a fixed ancilla Hilbert-space dimension, and a fixed number of outcomes $N=|Z|=|P|$, find the joint observables $Z$ that are most efficient for programming POVMs, namely those minimizing
\[
\varepsilon(Z)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_N}\min_{Q\in\mathcal M_{Z,A}}\delta(P,Q),
\]
where $\mathcal P_N$ is the convex set of $N$-outcome POVMs, $\mathcal M_{Z,A}=\{\operatorname{tr}_2[(I\otimes\sigma)Z]:\sigma\in A\}$ is the programmable set associated with $Z$ and ancilla state space $A$, and
\[
\delta(P,Q)=\max_{\rho}\sum_i\left|\operatorname{tr}\bigl[\rho(P_i-Q_i)\bigr]\right|.
\]
The report states that the solution is unknown even for $d=2$.

title: Unconditional instability of an explicit partitioned fluid–structure scheme
statement_utf8:
For the axisymmetric potential-flow/thin-elastic-tube model on $\Omega=\{(z,r)\in\mathbb{R}^2:0<z<L,\ 0<r<R\}$, with interface $\Sigma=\overline\Omega\cap\{r=R\}$, the explicit partitioned time-marching scheme obtained by discretizing the structure equation with leap-frog and the fluid equations with implicit Euler is unconditionally unstable whenever
\[
\frac{\rho_s h_s}{\rho_f\,\mu_{\max}}<1,
\]
where $\rho_f$ and $\rho_s$ are the fluid and structure densities, $h_s$ is the structure thickness, and $\mu_{\max}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the added-mass operator $M_A$. title: Minimum degree of a nonzero difference of powers
statement_utf8:

It states that the drop from the common top degree is at most $r-1$, equivalently
\[
\deg(P^m-Q^n)\ge m\deg P-r+1.
